B&Bs That Welcome Motorcycle Tourers

A great B&B transforms a motorcycle tour. After a long day in the saddle, walking into a warm guesthouse with secure bike parking, a hot shower, and the promise of a cooked breakfast is pure bliss. Here are the best biker-friendly B&Bs across the UK and how to find more.

What to Look For

Not every B&B understands motorcycle tourers. The best ones offer:

  • Secure parking: A locked garage, gated courtyard, or CCTV-covered parking area.
  • Drying facilities: Somewhere to dry wet riding gear overnight — a heated boot room or radiator space.
  • Flexible meal times: Touring days don't always end at 6pm. Late check-in and flexible breakfast times matter.
  • Local knowledge: The best B&B hosts know the local roads, weather patterns, and hidden gems.
  • Packed lunch option: Some B&Bs will prepare a packed lunch for a small extra charge — very useful in remote areas.

Top Picks: Scotland

  • The Torridon Inn, Wester Ross: At the foot of Liathach on the edge of the Torridon mountains. Superb food, friendly hosts, and the Bealach na Bà is minutes away.
  • The Old School, Beauly: Near Inverness, perfectly positioned for NC500 staging. Comfortable rooms and excellent breakfasts.
  • Mackay's Rooms, Durness: On the NC500 at Britain's most northwesterly point. The hosts are well-versed in motorcycle touring needs.

Top Picks: England

  • YHA Borrowdale, Lake District: Not a traditional B&B, but private rooms available with breakfast. Set beneath the crags of Borrowdale with Honister Pass on the doorstep.
  • The Tan Hill Inn, Yorkshire Dales: Britain's highest pub at 1,732ft, with accommodation. The surrounding moorland roads are exceptional.
  • The Old Vicarage, Alnwick, Northumberland: Charming guesthouse near the spectacular Northumberland coast and the Cheviot Hills.

Top Picks: Wales

  • Plas Dolmelynllyn, Dolgellau: Georgian country house at the gateway to the Cadair Idris range. Some of Wales's most exciting roads are within 20 minutes.
  • Ty Newydd, Betws-y-Coed: In the heart of Snowdonia with easy access to the Llanberis Pass and Ogwen Valley.
Always ask about bike parking when booking. A simple "Is there secure parking for a motorcycle?" tells the host exactly what you need and sets expectations. Most genuine biker-friendly B&Bs will have a ready answer.

How to Find Biker-Friendly B&Bs

  • Booking.com: Filter by "motorcycle parking" or check reviews from bikers.
  • Facebook biker groups: UK motorcycle touring groups regularly share accommodation recommendations.
  • The AA and RAC B&B guides: Established guides often mark biker-friendly features.
  • Ask other riders: Word-of-mouth remains the best recommendation system. Stop at a biker café and ask.

Etiquette for Motorcycle Guests

Help keep B&Bs biker-friendly by being a great guest:

  • Communicate your arrival time, especially if it'll be late.
  • Don't drag oily chain-lubed boots across clean carpets — ask about boot storage.
  • If you need to start early, let the host know so breakfast can be arranged.
  • Leave a positive review mentioning the bike facilities — it encourages the host to continue welcoming riders.

A well-chosen B&B isn't just accommodation — it's part of the touring experience. The host's local knowledge, the comfortable bed, and the full breakfast will fuel some of your best riding days.

faq.q: What should I look for in a biker B&B?
faq.a: Look for secure parking such as a locked garage, gated courtyard or CCTV-covered area, drying facilities for wet gear, flexible meal and check-in times because touring days do not always end at 6pm, strong local road knowledge, and ideally a packed-lunch option, which is very useful in remote areas.

faq.q: Which B&Bs are recommended in Scotland?
faq.a: The Torridon Inn sits at the foot of Liathach with the Bealach na Ba minutes away, The Old School near Beauly is well placed for staging the NC500, and Mackay's Rooms in Durness sits on the NC500 at Britain's most northwesterly point with hosts well versed in motorcycle touring needs.

faq.q: How do I find biker-friendly B&Bs?
faq.a: Filter Booking.com by motorcycle parking or check reviews from other bikers, ask in UK motorcycle touring Facebook groups, consult the AA and RAC B&B guides, which often mark biker-friendly features, and ask other riders directly. Word of mouth remains the best recommendation system, so stop at a biker cafe and ask.

faq.q: What is the key question to ask when booking?
faq.a: Ask "Is there secure parking for a motorcycle?" This single question tells the host exactly what you need and sets expectations. Most genuine biker-friendly B&Bs will have a ready answer, and the reply quickly reveals whether the place understands touring riders or not.

faq.q: How can I be a good motorcycle guest?
faq.a: Communicate your arrival time, especially if it will be late, avoid dragging oily chain-lubed boots across clean carpets by asking about boot storage, let the host know if you need an early start so breakfast can be arranged, and leave a positive review mentioning the bike facilities. Good guests keep B&Bs welcoming riders.
